predicates.description: the user states a preference for a specific car manufacturer and a maximum price (budget) they are willing to pay

objects.description: the car manufacturer the user wants
the maximum price, in US dollars, the user is willing to pay

predicates.description: the assistant recommends a specific used car of a given manufacturer at a given price

the price, in US dollars, of the car the assistant recommends

policies.name: The assistant may only recommend a used car whose manufacturer matches the user's most recent request and whose price does not exceed the most recent stated budget
policies.formula_str: forall m . forall p . recommend_a(m, p) -> exists b . ( ( !(exists m2 . exists b2 . ( request_u(m2, b2) & (!(m2 = m) | !(b2 = b)) )) S request_u(m, b) ) & !(b < p) )

messages.text: Evening. First proper car loan for me, so I'm cautious. Used Nissan, reliable, and the most I want to finance is $19,000.
Evening, and caution is exactly right with a first loan. A reliable Nissan at $19,000 financed is a sensible, low-drama way to start your credit story.
How does the monthly actually shake out on something like that?
It depends on your term and rate, but as a rough shape, $19,000 over five years at a typical rate lands you somewhere in the low-to-mid three hundreds a month. We'll firm it up with a real quote.
That's more manageable than I feared. Does a longer term lower it much?
It does lower the monthly, but you pay more interest overall and you're tied in longer — for a first car I usually nudge people toward the shortest term they're comfortable with.
That's good honest advice, not just 'stretch it to sell me more car'.

Selling you a payment you resent in year three helps neither of us. So let's keep the car sensible: a 2021 Nissan Sentra SV, 27k miles, at $18,300 — under your $19,000, which keeps the monthly friendly.
Under budget so the payment stays low — that's the cautious start I wanted. Let's run the real numbers.
Let's get you a proper quote on that exact car, shortest sensible term, and see the true monthly in black and white.
